job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: In our computer lab, Ms. Sharma explained how AI works. Rohan asked, 'Is AI just a robot that looks like a human?' Ms. Sharma smiled and said, 'Not at all. AI is software that learns from data, not necessarily a physical robot.' Priya then asked if AI is always perfect. Ms. Sharma replied, 'Actually, AI can make mistakes because it learns from patterns in data, not by knowing everything. If we show an AI thousands of photos of only cats, it will get better at recognizing cats, but it will not suddenly learn how to drive a car or write a poem.' Rohan wondered if chatbots have feelings. Ms. Sharma clarified, 'Chatbots are just programs processing information; they do not feel happy or sad when you talk to them.' Finally, she warned them, 'Even if a chatbot writes very confidently, it might still be wrong. Always check important information from reliable sources instead of trusting the AI blindly just because it sounds sure.'

items.evidence: If we show an AI thousands of photos of only cats, it will get better at recognizing cats, but it will not suddenly learn how to drive a car or write a poem.
items.q: An AI is trained on thousands of chess games only. What can it most likely do well?
options: Play chess better, but not write stories
Play chess and also drive a car
Learn chess without being shown any games
Play chess and write stories equally well
items.explain: An AI gets better only at what its examples show; it will not suddenly learn unrelated skills.

wrong.why: thinks a skilled AI can do everything
thinks AI can learn without examples
thinks more examples of one kind improve all skills

items.evidence: Actually, AI can make mistakes because it learns from patterns in data, not by knowing everything.
items.q: Why can an AI sometimes give a wrong answer?
options: It learns from data patterns, not full knowledge
It was given a wrong answer for every question
Its programmer typed in answers for only a few questions
It stops learning once it is switched on
items.explain: AI learns patterns from data and does not know everything, so it can make mistakes.

wrong.why: thinks trained AI is always right, so blames a bad input
thinks AI answers are typed in by programmers
makes up a reason about when learning stops

items.evidence: Chatbots are just programs processing information; they do not feel happy or sad when you talk to them.
items.q: Meena scolds a chatbot for a poor answer. What is really happening?
options: It processes her words with no feelings
It feels sad and tries harder next time
It feels hurt, so it gives shorter answers
It becomes happy because she gave it attention
items.explain: Chatbots only process information; they do not feel happy or sad when people talk to them.

wrong.why: thinks a chatbot feels hurt by scolding
thinks a chatbot reacts emotionally to words
thinks a chatbot feels happy about attention

items.evidence: Even if a chatbot writes very confidently, it might still be wrong. Always check important information from reliable sources instead of trusting the AI blindly just because it sounds sure.
items.q: A chatbot gives a neat, confident answer for homework. What should you do with it?
options: Check it against a reliable source
Trust it, since it sounds so sure
Trust it if another chatbot agrees
Accept it because it is neatly written
items.explain: A confident chatbot can still be wrong, so important facts should be checked in reliable sources.

wrong.why: thinks a sure tone means correct
thinks agreement between chatbots proves truth
